For the 4 x 300yds. we were in a quandary as Jim Tosh was unable to run owing to sickness and so we brought in Stroud, who had already raced twice on that evening.
Stroud showed himself to be in fine trim so early in the season, and annexed both sprints.

Stroud, who was second in this race, proved how fit he is by running away with the 220 yards match event, and must now be considered one of our leading sprinters.

George Basford ran next and maintained this lead; Stroud on the next 220 had Pallett as his opponent and as they had to cross at the finish in order to reach their waiting club-mates, (Herne Hill were drawn No. 1 with ourselves No. 4), the Herne Hill half-miler Thorpe went off about a yard in front of Tommy Scrimshaw.

Probably the best feat of the evening was that of Arthur Penny in winning the two miles run from scratch; whilst the performances of Don Brown in the Walk, Stroud in the 220 yards, and Ellis in the Shot Putt were very creditable.

Odell could only finish third, and another fine sprinter, Stroud, won the title in quite good time.
Stroud and E.
Kealey and Stroud were our hopes in the 100 yards match. The former finished second, with Stroud close up, fourth; but T.V.H. had first and third and so gained a two-points lead.
In the fourth of the six events, held at the "Kinnaird" meeting, a relay 4 x 220 yards, were placed third, Stroud, Kealey, Pack and Basford forming our team.

The 4 x 300 yards was in the nature of a tragedy for us; for with Stroud going first, and Bennett continuing the good work, we saw Michael having a neck and neck race with the Croydon man over the third stage.
Stroud and Brodie also showed us some speed; whilst one of our younger members, F. Skelley, gave indication of first-class performances to come.

On May 25th, at the White City, was held the 4 x 220 yds. and we fielded a useful team in Kealey, Stroud, Mewes and Michael. Kealey elected to start for us, and drawing number 1 station, he was twice bumped very badly and so we lost any advantage which we might have had.
In the 100 Yards match, Tavender, of T.V.H., just pipped Brodie in 10 2/5 secs., and with Stroud filling third place we managed to share points in this event.

Eddie Pack ran the 440 yards stage and did well in handing over third behind Whittingham and Pallett. Stroud and Bone both did their bit in keeping this position; and Tommy went off about 30 yards behind the leaders, who were A.

As a point of interest we had three members in the first twelve in the Civil Service Championship, viz: Baulch, Stroud and Hallowell. I would also like to congratulate Jack Brown on notching yet another championship win over the country.

Newell and Stroud were 4th. and 7th. respectively in the 1500 metres, Newell's time being 3m.58s. Alan Jackson and Dudley Gordon were finalists in the 400m. and a welcome entry in the 400m. hurdles was Brian Coleman.
